established_findings.statement: Large language models are actively applied to NetOps/AIOps tasks (intent-to-configuration translation, configuration synthesis, fault diagnosis, and limited self-healing) in prototype studies and surveys.
limitations: Most work is prototype or experimental rather than large-scale production deployments.
Evaluations often use limited task sets or synthetic/small-scale environments.

established_findings.statement: Operational reliability of LLM-driven NetOps depends principally on surrounding architecture (validators, tool scaffolding, assurance contracts, and human-in-the-loop) rather than model outputs alone.
limitations: Argument is supported by architectural analyses and prototypes rather than controlled causal experiments isolating each component.
Degree to which each surrounding mechanism (e.g., human approval vs. automated verifier) contributes to reliability varies by study and is not standardized.

established_findings.statement: Tool-augmented agent architectures (external APIs/tools, Toolformer-style self-supervision, API-Bank, and retrieval-augmented generation) demonstrably improve LLM task capabilities and are a prominent research direction for NetOps tooling and verification.
limitations: Benchmarks and tool suites vary; improvements shown on specific tasks/benchmarks may not transfer automatically to complex, multi-vendor NetOps workflows.
Tool integration adds operational complexity (latency, error modes) that requires careful evaluation.

established_findings.statement: Hallucination/fabrication remains a significant failure mode for LLMs and is an active area of detection and mitigation research.
limitations: Rates and forms of hallucination depend on model, prompt, domain, and mitigation strategy; studies use varied metrics.
Detection/mitigation methods reduce but do not eliminate hallucination according to supplied records.

established_findings.statement: Generate–validate–repair and RAG-style grounding, sometimes using network simulators/validators (e.g., Batfish in prototypes), are proposed and used as mitigation patterns to check or sandbox LLM-generated network changes.
limitations: Use of validators like Batfish is reported in prototypes; comprehensive evaluations of end-to-end effectiveness against diverse misconfigurations are limited in the supplied records.
Integration and oracle accuracy of validators vary by scenario.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent current LLM-based NetOps systems generalize reliably across multi-vendor equipment, large production topologies, and adversarial perturbations remains unresolved.
limitations: Supplied evidence highlights concerns and adversarial methodologies but does not provide comprehensive cross-vendor production-scale evaluations.
Empirical results addressing this question are sparse in the provided record set.

unresolved_questions.statement: Whether fully autonomous LLM-agent remediation (closed-loop changes without human approval) can meet operational safety, auditability, and regulatory requirements in production is unresolved.
limitations: Records propose governance and compliance-aware architectures but do not report real-world regulated production deployments proving full compliance.
Regulatory acceptability depends on external factors (auditors, standards) not addressed empirically in the supplied set.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is no widely-accepted public benchmark in the supplied records that evaluates agentic NetOps systems end-to-end with workflow-centered criteria (trace quality, sandbox replay, canary trials, rollback-aware scoring).
limitations: API-Bank and other tool benchmarks exist but focus on tool use generally rather than a standardized, NetOps-specific workflow-centered evaluation as described.
Absence claim is limited to the supplied record set.

candidate_gaps.statement: Empirical studies that combine adversarial prompt‑injection/red‑teaming with NetOps configuration‑generation plus validator/repair loops are limited in the supplied records.
limitations: Adversarial and prompt-injection studies are present, and NetOps prototypes are present, but few supplied works combine both in systematic, quantitative experiments.
This gap statement is bounded to the supplied record list and may not reflect the entire literature beyond these records.

excluded_claims: LLM-driven NetOps systems in the supplied records are proven production-ready for fully autonomous, vendor-diverse, safety-certified remediation (unsupported by provided evidence).
Any single supplied record demonstrates elimination of hallucination in LLM outputs for NetOps tasks (no supplied record shows complete elimination).
There is a widely-adopted, community standard benchmark that fully measures workflow-level safety and rollback-aware performance for agentic NetOps (not present in supplied records).
